import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.48

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

A locally finite group is called an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups
are abelian. Does every variety of $A$-groups have a finite basis of
identities?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.48»

/-- A group identity in countably many variables is a pair of words in the
free group on those variables. -/
abbrev GroupIdentity := FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A group satisfies an identity if the two words have equal values under
every assignment of its variables. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (e : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift x e.1 = FreeGroup.lift x e.2

/-- A group satisfies a set of identities if it satisfies each member. -/
def SatisfiesIdentities (G : Type*) [Group G] (T : Set GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ T, SatisfiesIdentity G e

/-- A group is locally finite if each of its finitely generated subgroups is
finite. -/
def IsLocallyFiniteGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- An $A$-group is a locally finite group all of whose Sylow subgroups are
abelian. -/
def IsAGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsLocallyFiniteGroup G ∧
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, IsMulCommutative P

/--
Does every variety of $A$-groups possess a finite basis of identities?

Here `T` is an arbitrary identity presentation of a group variety. A finite
basis is a finite set `B` of identities having exactly the same group models
as `T`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.48» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ T : Set GroupIdentity,
      (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SatisfiesIdentities G T → IsAGroup G) →
      ∃ B : Set GroupIdentity, B.Finite ∧
        ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
          SatisfiesIdentities G B ↔ SatisfiesIdentities G T := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.48»
modeling_decisions: Represented a group identity as a pair of words in the free group on countably many variables; every ordinary group identity uses only finitely many of these variables.
Represented a group variety by an arbitrary set T of identities through its class of group models. A finite basis is a finite set B with exactly the same models as T.
Defined local finiteness by requiring every finitely generated subgroup to be finite.
Used Mathlib's Sylow p G, which is defined as a maximal p-subgroup, and restricted p to primes. Abelianity of a Sylow subgroup is expressed by IsMulCommutative.
Formalized the source's phrase 'variety of A-groups' directly: every group model of T must be locally finite and have abelian Sylow subgroups.

/-!
# Conjecture 4.48

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

A locally finite group is called an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups are abelian.
Does every variety of $A$-groups have a finite basis of identities?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.48»

universe u

/-- A group identity in countably many variables, represented by its two words. -/
abbrev GroupIdentity := FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A group satisfies an identity if its two words have equal values under every assignment of
its variables. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type u) [Group G] (identity : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ valuation : ℕ → G,
    FreeGroup.lift valuation identity.1 = FreeGroup.lift valuation identity.2

/-- A group is locally finite if each of its finitely generated subgroups is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFiniteGroup (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- An $A$-group is a locally finite group whose Sylow subgroups are all abelian. -/
def IsAGroup (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsLocallyFiniteGroup G ∧
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, IsMulCommutative P

/--
Does every variety of $A$-groups possess a finite basis of identities?

Here a variety is represented by a set of group identities defining its members. A finite basis
is a finite set of identities defining exactly the same groups. An $A$-group is locally finite and
has abelian Sylow (maximal $p$-) subgroups for every prime $p$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.48» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ identities : Set GroupIdentity,
      (∀ (G : Type u) [Group G],
        (∀ identity ∈ identities, SatisfiesIdentity G identity) → IsAGroup G) →
      ∃ basis : Set GroupIdentity, basis.Finite ∧
        ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G],
          (∀ identity ∈ identities, SatisfiesIdentity G identity) ↔
            ∀ identity ∈ basis, SatisfiesIdentity G identity := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.48»
modeling_decisions: A group identity is represented by a pair of words in the free group on countably many variables. Every such word uses only finitely many variables, so this captures ordinary finitary group identities.

A variety is represented by an arbitrary set of group identities through the class of all group models satisfying those identities. A finite basis is a finite set of identities with exactly the same group models.
Local finiteness is stated as finiteness of every finitely generated subgroup, using Mathlib's `Subgroup.FG` and `Finite`.

Sylow subgroups are Mathlib's `Sylow p G`, whose definition is a maximal `p`-subgroup and applies to infinite groups. The A-group condition quantifies over prime `p` and requires `IsMulCommutative P` for every such Sylow subgroup.
The model condition is universe-polymorphic: at each universe level, every model of the defining identities must be an A-group and the original and finite bases must have the same models.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.48

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

A locally finite group is said to be an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups are
abelian. Does every variety of $A$-groups possess a finite basis of identities?

Here a Sylow $p$-subgroup of an arbitrary group is a maximal $p$-subgroup (`Sylow p G`).
An identity (law) is a word $w$ in the free group on countably many variables
$x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group $G$ satisfies $w$ if $w$ becomes $1$ under every substitution of
elements of $G$ for the variables. The variety defined by a set $S$ of identities is the
class of all groups satisfying every identity in $S$. A variety of $A$-groups is a variety
all of whose members are $A$-groups. A basis of identities of a variety is a set $T$ of
identities defining the same variety.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.48»

/-- A group $G$ is locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- A locally finite group is an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups are abelian, that
is, for every prime $p$ every maximal $p$-subgroup is abelian. -/
def IsAGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsLocallyFinite G ∧ ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, IsMulCommutative P

/-- A group $G$ satisfies the identity (law) $w$, a word in the free group on the countably
many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$, if $w$ becomes $1$ under every substitution of elements of
$G$ for the variables, i.e. every homomorphism from the free group to $G$ sends $w$ to $1$. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, f w = 1

/-- A group $G$ belongs to the variety defined by the set $S$ of identities if $G$ satisfies
every identity in $S$. -/
def MemVariety (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ S, SatisfiesIdentity G w

/-- Every finite abelian group is an $A$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isAGroup_of_finite_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] [Finite G] : IsAGroup G :=
  ⟨fun _ _ => inferInstance, fun _ _ _ => inferInstance⟩

/-- A group satisfies the commutator identity $[x_0, x_1]$ if and only if it is abelian. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesIdentity_commutator_iff (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    SatisfiesIdentity G ⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆ ↔ ∀ a b : G, a * b = b * a := by
  constructor
  · intro h a b
    have := h (FreeGroup.lift fun n => if n = 0 then a else b)
    simpa [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm] using this
  · intro h f
    simp [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm, h]

/--
A locally finite group is said to be an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups are
abelian. Does every variety of $A$-groups possess a finite basis of identities?

That is, for every set $S$ of identities such that every group satisfying $S$ is an
$A$-group, is there a finite set $T$ of identities defining the same variety, i.e. such
that a group satisfies $S$ if and only if it satisfies $T$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.48» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ),
      (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], MemVariety S G → IsAGroup G) →
      ∃ T : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ),
        ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], MemVariety S G ↔ MemVariety (T : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.48»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is correct: the first sentence only defines 'A-group' and the second poses the sole yes/no question.
modeling_decisions: A variety is represented by a defining set S of identities (words in FreeGroup ℕ, countably many variables), following the standard (Neumann) definition of a variety as the class of all groups satisfying a set of laws, rather than via Birkhoff's HSP closure characterization.
'Variety of A-groups' is read as: every group in the variety is an A-group (∀ G : Type, MemVariety S G → IsAGroup G), as in the decomposition notes; not as 'the variety generated by some A-groups'.
'Possesses a finite basis of identities' is read as: ∃ T : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ) such that a group satisfies S iff it satisfies T (T defines the same variety).

Groups are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following repository convention (1_40, 19_25). This loses nothing: varieties are determined by their countable members, and the A-group property (local finiteness, abelian Sylow subgroups) is detected on finitely generated subgroups, which are countable.

Sylow subgroups are Mathlib's `Sylow p G` (maximal p-subgroups, appropriate for locally finite/infinite groups), quantified over primes p only; without the primality restriction `IsPGroup 0 G` holds for every G and would wrongly force G abelian.
Locally finite is defined as every finitely generated subgroup (Subgroup.FG) being Finite.

Two short `@[category API]` lemmas were added as basic tests of the bespoke definitions (finite abelian groups are A-groups; the commutator word is satisfied exactly by abelian groups), per CONTRIBUTING's request for API tests of bespoke definitions.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.48

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

A locally finite group is said to be an *$A$-group* if all of its Sylow subgroups are
abelian. Does every variety of $A$-groups possess a finite basis of identities?

Here a Sylow $p$-subgroup of an arbitrary group is a maximal $p$-subgroup (Mathlib's
`Sylow p G`). An identity (law) is a word $w$ in the free group on countably many letters
$x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group $G$ satisfies $w$ if $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every substitution of
elements of $G$ for the letters. A variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying
some set of identities, and a variety of $A$-groups is a variety all of whose members are
$A$-groups. Such a variety possesses a finite basis of identities if it is the class of all
groups satisfying some *finite* set of identities.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 4.48
-/

universe u

namespace Kourovka.«4.48»

/-- A group `G` satisfies the identity (law) `w`, a word in the free group on the countably
many letters $x_0, x_1, \dots$, if `w` evaluates to `1` under every substitution of elements
of `G` for the letters, i.e. under every homomorphism `FreeGroup ℕ →* G`. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, f w = 1

/-- A class of groups `𝒱` is a variety if it consists exactly of the groups satisfying
some set `W` of identities. -/
def IsVariety (𝒱 : (G : Type u) → [Group G] → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], 𝒱 G ↔ ∀ w ∈ W, SatisfiesLaw G w

/-- A class of groups `𝒱` possesses a finite basis of identities if it consists exactly of the
groups satisfying some finite set `W` of identities. -/
def HasFiniteBasis (𝒱 : (G : Type u) → [Group G] → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ W : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ), ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], 𝒱 G ↔ ∀ w ∈ W, SatisfiesLaw G w

/-- A group is locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFiniteGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- A locally finite group is an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups are abelian, where a
Sylow $p$-subgroup ($p$ prime) is a maximal $p$-subgroup. -/
def IsAGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsLocallyFiniteGroup G ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, IsMulCommutative P

/-- A group satisfies the identity `1` (which is trivially satisfied by every group). -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesLaw_one (G : Type*) [Group G] : SatisfiesLaw G 1 :=
  fun f => map_one f

/-- A group satisfies the commutator identity $[x_0, x_1]$ if and only if it is abelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesLaw_commutator_iff (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    SatisfiesLaw G ⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆ ↔ IsMulCommutative G := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨⟨fun x y => ?_⟩⟩
    have := h (FreeGroup.lift fun n => if n = 0 then x else y)
    simpa [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm] using this
  · intro h f
    rw [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm]
    exact mul_comm _ _

/-- A class of groups possessing a finite basis of identities is a variety. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem HasFiniteBasis.isVariety {𝒱 : (G : Type u) → [Group G] → Prop}
    (h : HasFiniteBasis 𝒱) : IsVariety 𝒱 := by
  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := h
  exact ⟨↑W, fun G _ => by simpa using hW G⟩

/-- Every finite group is locally finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLocallyFiniteGroup_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsLocallyFiniteGroup G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- Every finite abelian group is an $A$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isAGroup_of_finite_of_isMulCommutative (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] [Finite G] :
    IsAGroup G :=
  ⟨isLocallyFiniteGroup_of_finite G, fun _ _ _ => ⟨⟨fun x y => Subtype.ext (mul_comm x.1 y.1)⟩⟩⟩

/--
A locally finite group is said to be an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups are abelian.
Does every variety of $A$-groups (i.e. every variety of groups all of whose members are
$A$-groups) possess a finite basis of identities?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.48» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ 𝒱 : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop, IsVariety 𝒱 →
      (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒱 G → IsAGroup G) → HasFiniteBasis 𝒱 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.48»

I concur with the note that 'variety of A-groups' should be read as a variety all of whose members are A-groups (such a variety is locally finite and is generated by its finite members, which are finite A-groups); the alternative reading 'variety generated by A-groups' is recorded under modeling decisions.
modeling_decisions: 'Variety of A-groups' is read (per the decomposition table) as a variety all of whose members are A-groups, i.e. `∀ G, 𝒱 G → IsAGroup G`. An alternative reading, 'variety generated by A-groups', would be a different (larger) class of varieties — e.g. it would include the variety of all abelian groups, which is not locally finite; the table's reading was followed.

A variety is defined à la Hanna Neumann as the class of all groups satisfying some set of identities (laws), with laws taken as elements of `FreeGroup ℕ` (free group on countably many letters x₀, x₁, …). def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- A group identity is an equation between two words in countably many variables. -/
abbrev GroupIdentity := FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A group satisfies an identity if the two words have equal values under every assignment of
its variables. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (e : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift x e.1 = FreeGroup.lift x e.2

/-- A group models a set of identities if it satisfies each identity in the set. -/
def ModelsIdentities (G : Type*) [Group G] (E : Set GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ E, SatisfiesIdentity G e

/-- A group is locally finite if each of its finitely generated subgroups is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFiniteGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- An $A$-group is a locally finite group all of whose Sylow subgroups are abelian. -/
def IsAGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsLocallyFiniteGroup G ∧
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, IsMulCommutative P

/--
Does every variety of $A$-groups possess a finite basis of identities?

Here a variety presented by a set `E` of group identities consists of all groups that model `E`.
Thus, `E` presents a variety of $A$-groups when every group modeling `E` is an $A$-group. A finite
basis is a finite set of identities with exactly the same group models.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.48» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ E : Set GroupIdentity,
      (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], ModelsIdentities G E → IsAGroup G) →
        ∃ B : Set GroupIdentity, B.Finite ∧
          ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], ModelsIdentities G B ↔ ModelsIdentities G E := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.48»
modeling_decisions: A group identity is represented as a pair of words in the free group on countably many variables; a group satisfies it when all variable assignments give equal values.
A variety is represented by an arbitrary set of group identities through its class of group models. A finite basis is a finite identity set with exactly the same group models.
A locally finite group is defined as one whose finitely generated subgroups are finite.
An A-group is required to be locally finite and to have every Sylow p-subgroup abelian, quantifying over prime natural numbers and Mathlib's maximal p-subgroups.
The theorem quantifies over `Type`-small groups, following repository idiom; identity equivalence can in any case be detected on countable quotients of the countably generated free group.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.48

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

A locally finite group is called an $A$-group if all its Sylow subgroups are
abelian. Does every variety of $A$-groups have a finite basis of identities?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.48»

/-- A group is locally finite if each of its finitely generated subgroups is
finite. -/
def IsLocallyFiniteGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- An $A$-group is a locally finite group all of whose Sylow subgroups are
abelian. -/
def IsAGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsLocallyFiniteGroup G ∧
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, IsMulCommutative P

/-- A group $G$ satisfies an identity $u = v$ in countably many variables if
every assignment of the variables to elements of $G$ gives equal values for
$u$ and $v$. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G]
    (identity : FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f identity.1 = FreeGroup.lift f identity.2

/-- A group satisfies a set of identities if it satisfies every identity in
the set. -/
def SatisfiesIdentities (G : Type*) [Group G]
    (identities : Set (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ identity ∈ identities, SatisfiesIdentity G identity

/--
Does every variety of $A$-groups possess a finite basis of identities?

Here a group variety is represented by a set `identities` of group identities,
with its members being exactly the groups satisfying those identities. An
$A$-group is locally finite and has abelian Sylow subgroups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.48» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ identities : Set (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ),
      (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], SatisfiesIdentities G identities → IsAGroup G) →
      ∃ basis : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ),
        ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
          SatisfiesIdentities G identities ↔
            ∀ identity ∈ basis, SatisfiesIdentity G identity := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.48»
modeling_decisions: A group variety is represented extensionally as the class of groups satisfying a set of identities; the theorem quantifies over all such sets of identities.
Group identities are pairs of words in `FreeGroup ℕ`. Countably many variables suffice because every group word uses only finitely many variables.
The source's definition of an A-group is encoded directly: every finitely generated subgroup is finite, and every Sylow p-subgroup for prime p is commutative.

A finite basis is represented by a `Finset` of identities whose models are exactly the models of the original set. It is not required syntactically to be a subset of the original presentation, as is standard for a basis of a variety.
As in nearby repository statements, model quantification uses `G : Type` (small group types). Identity classes and failures of the A-group conditions are detected at this universe level.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: `Subgroup.FG` supplies finitely generated subgroups, and `Finite` supplies finiteness; the new definition combines these as every finitely generated subgroup being finite.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `Sylow p G` already represents maximal p-subgroups for arbitrary groups, and `IsMulCommutative P` expresses that the subgroup is abelian.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: `FreeGroup.lift` evaluates a free-group word under an assignment of variables, so the definition universally equates evaluations of the two sides.
